brief: Lane rb3: R3 of hybrid continuous batching for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 on CUDA (DGX Spark GB10): (a) one GDN and attention launch for all batch rows with per-row state tables, (b) device-side top-k sampling, (c) CUDA graph per row count and per-state solo graphs, (d) prefill/decode overlap; decode stays row-exact (bitwise to solo). Targets: above 140 tok/s at 4 streams, about 200 at 16. User approved R3 and the loader free-memory PR; busy chunk 2048 default.
hypothesis: After rb2 the batched step ran at model-loop speed but 25% (B=4) and 42% (B=16) of it were per-row GDN/attention launches and the step was eager; one row-table launch per op plus a graph per row count should cut the step by about 15% at B=4 and 20% at B=16, enough for 140 and 200 tok/s, with every row still bitwise the solo step.

summary: R3 (a)+(c) done and gated: one row-table launch per op for all batch rows (GDN conv/delta rule, KV append, rope, split-KV attention) and a CUDA graph per row count, every row still bitwise the solo step. 35B aggregate decode, 1k prompt, 3 bursts, same session, main 6ca51a19 as baseline: 4 streams 122.4 to 141.2 tok/s (above the 140 target on the mean, worst burst 139.3), 16 streams 167.1 to 194.6 (target about 200), 4 streams with 4k prompts 83.0 to 91.3, 1 stream 73.2 to 73.3 (no regression). Device top-k sampling (b) is exact and on by default: a sampled batched step is 33% (B=4) and 25% (B=16) cheaper. Prefill/decode overlap (d) is bitwise and cuts ITL p99 at 16 streams from 500 to 75-150 ms but costs 8-15% aggregate, so it stays opt-in. The first speed run showed no gain because serve selects admitted kernels only and the row-table twins were never swept; fixed by inheriting the twin's admission.
lessons: Run the speed matrix through serve before believing a kernel PR: tests run without admission, serve selects admitted kernels only, and the new row-table kernels silently fell back to per-row launches until they inherited their twin's admission.

On the GB10 a prefill chunk and decode both stream the weights, so overlapping them lowers aggregate throughput (4 streams 141 to 130 tok/s, last prefill done at 1.38 s instead of 0.88 s) while improving ITL; the shared resource is memory bandwidth, not the schedule.

A CUDA graph capture on a decode stream tolerates ordinary calls from a prefill thread; the failure was the test running solo reference steps (same stream, own graphs) in the prefill process. Hard-coded stream 0 in one launch (top-k) produced garbage only under overlap.

Device top-k sampling is exact when the kernel returns the sampler's own candidate order (value descending, ties by index) because the host walk touches only those k candidates; a sampled step at B=16 drops from 72.7 to 54.9 ms.
localeval aggregates one burst per invocation: run each multi-stream cell as separate invocations to see the spread (4 streams spans 139.3 to 144.5 here), a single burst cannot decide a 140 target.
